svg.title: SAGE architecture — governed memory, durable coordination, explicit trust boundaries
svg.desc: Agents use authenticated MCP or REST. Memory and local policy transactions pass through CometBFT and ABCI to authoritative BadgerDB, then project to SQL at Commit. Message claims, replies and wakes use a separate node-local coordination store. CEREBRUM is the local human control plane. Peer federation is separate from same-chain validator consensus.
svg.text: SAGE / ARCHITECTURE
Memory and work, with different guarantees.
v11.19.13 behavior · app-v27 ceiling · personal node or governed multi-validator chain
AI agents & integrations
MCP clients · Python SDK · signed REST
Exact agent identity; runtime sessions coordinate work, not authority.
CEREBRUM · local human
Approval, policy, recovery, observability
Loopback control plane; separate Root authority
Admission & live policy
Identity · active enrollment · role / profile · ownership / groups / grants · classification · hard denials
01 / CONSENSUS MEMORY & LOCAL POLICY
02 / NODE-LOCAL COORDINATION
Signed transactions → CometBFT → ABCI
Ordered execution; validators submit memory acceptance votes.
BadgerDB · authoritative chain state
Hashes, lifecycle, votes, local RBAC, ownership, app-version rules
Commit-time SQL projection
SQLite (personal) / PostgreSQL + pgvector (cluster)
Content + vectors → authorized recall; not the policy authority
Inbox · claims · replies · history
Durable coordination; message payloads are not memory writes.
Session + revision-fenced handoff
Same signed agent; explicit takeover; recover retained claims
Node-local SQLite coordination store
Idempotent results + local wake sequence; wakes carry no payload.
Task notices point back to consensus-backed, assigned tasks.
Same-chain validators ≠ federated peers
Personal: one real validator, no Byzantine redundancy.
Multi-validator: CometBFT orders one shared chain;
BFT assumes less than ⅓ faulty voting power.
Federation · separate SAGE chains
Explicit peer trust + exports / Read / Copy policy.
Authenticated messages; receiver-controlled memory Copy.
No implied local Write, membership, or Root authority.
Block inclusion ≠ memory acceptance. A task assignment ≠ a message claim. A wake ≠ delivery or read evidence.
